name: Glaucoma Guardian
tagline: Diagnosis, Monitoring, and Management of Glaucoma
description: A 15-episode series covering every clinical decision point in glaucoma care — from IOP and gonioscopy through OCT and visual fields to first-line therapy and surgical referral.

episodes.title: Glaucoma & IOP: The Only Risk Factor You Can Control
episodes.description:
What if you were slowly going blind and had absolutely no idea? That's the terrifying reality of glaucoma — a silent, painless disease that steals your vision before you ever notice something is wrong. In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down the pathophysiology of glaucoma in plain, accessible language, exploring exactly how elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) damages the optic nerve and why catching it early can mean the difference between sight and permanent vision loss.

We cover how aqueous humor is produced and drained inside the eye, what happens when that drainage system fails, and why rising IOP puts the optic nerve under dangerous mechanical stress. You'll learn why glaucoma is so difficult to detect without a comprehensive eye exam, and why age, genetics, race, and other risk factors — while significant — are completely beyond our control.

But here's the critical insight: intraocular pressure is the one modifiable risk factor in glaucoma. We explore the landmark research proving that lowering IOP reduces glaucoma risk by up to 50 percent, and walk through every major treatment approach available today — from prostaglandin eye drops and beta blockers to selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS).

Whether you're a patient, a caregiver, or simply someone who wants to protect their long-term eye health, this episode gives you the knowledge to take action. Because with glaucoma, what you don't know can genuinely cost you your vision.

Listen now, then visit Focuslinks.in for more eye health resources and episodes from Focus Cast.

episodes.title: Intraocular Pressure: Measurement, Diurnal Curve & Peak IOP
episodes.description:
Ever wondered what that puff of air at your eye exam is actually measuring? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down everything you need to know about intraocular pressure (IOP) — the vital sign your eyes cannot afford to ignore.

We start with the basics: what IOP is, how aqueous humor keeps your eye pressurized, and why elevated pressure is the leading driver of glaucoma, one of the world's top causes of irreversible blindness. From there, we walk you through the most trusted methods of measuring eye pressure — including Goldmann applanation tonometry, the non-contact air puff test, and the increasingly popular iCare tonometer — and explain why corneal thickness can change how your results are interpreted.

Then we dive into one of the most clinically important and often overlooked concepts in eye care: the diurnal curve. IOP is not a fixed number. It rises and falls throughout the day, typically peaking in the early morning hours when most patients are nowhere near a clinic. We explain why these pressure peaks matter more than averages, how the diurnal tension curve is used to capture the full picture, and how home tonometry is revolutionizing glaucoma monitoring by catching spikes that standard appointments miss entirely.

Whether you have been diagnosed with glaucoma, are considered a glaucoma suspect, or simply want to understand your eye health better, this episode gives you the knowledge to ask the right questions at your next appointment.

Listen now, and visit Focuslinks.in for more eye care resources and episodes of Focus Cast.

episodes.title: Gonioscopy in Glaucoma: Open, Closed & Plateau Angles
episodes.description:
What does the drainage angle of the eye actually look like — and what is it telling you about your patient's glaucoma? In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take a deep dive into gonioscopy, the essential clinical skill that gives you a direct window into the anterior chamber angle and transforms how you evaluate and manage glaucoma.

We start with the fundamentals — why total internal reflection makes the angle invisible without a special lens, and what a normal, healthy open angle looks like from Schwalbe's line all the way to the ciliary body band. From there, we walk through the urgent world of acute angle closure glaucoma, the silent danger of chronic angle closure, and the often-misunderstood plateau iris configuration versus plateau iris syndrome — a distinction that matters enormously when a laser iridotomy is not enough.

We also explore the wide spectrum of secondary angles, including neovascular glaucoma, pigment dispersion syndrome, pseudoexfoliation syndrome, and inflammatory and traumatic causes — each with its own gonioscopic signature that sharpens your diagnostic thinking. We wrap up with a practical look at the Shaffer and Spaeth grading systems and why systematic documentation makes all the difference over time.

Whether you are a medical student encountering gonioscopy for the first time or a clinician looking to sharpen your angle assessment skills, this episode breaks it all down in a way that is clear, clinically relevant, and genuinely engaging.

Listen now and start seeing the angle differently. Visit Focuslinks.in for more ophthalmology episodes and resources, and share this episode with a colleague who could use a gonioscopy refresher.

episodes.title: Optic Nerve Evaluation: Cup-to-Disc Ratio, RNFL & Disc Haemorrhages
episodes.description:
What does the optic disc really tell us — and are you reading it correctly? In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take a deep dive into optic nerve evaluation, one of the most critical and nuanced skills in clinical eye care. Whether you are preparing for your optometry or ophthalmology exams or looking to sharpen your fundus assessment technique, this episode breaks it all down in a way that is clear, practical, and genuinely fascinating.

We start with the cup-to-disc ratio — what is normal, what raises a red flag, and why a large CDR is not always pathological. From there, we explore the neuroretinal rim and the ISNT rule, explaining how subtle changes in rim tissue can be the earliest structural clue to glaucomatous damage. We then move into retinal nerve fiber layer defects, discussing how wedge-shaped RNFL loss often precedes visual field changes and how OCT has transformed our ability to detect these findings early. Finally, we cover disc haemorrhages — those easy-to-miss splinter bleeds that carry enormous clinical significance, particularly in normal tension glaucoma.

By the end of this episode, you will have a systematic framework for evaluating the optic disc with confidence, understanding not just what to look for, but why each finding matters. Because the optic nerve is not just part of the eye — it is a direct window into the brain, and learning to read it is one of the most powerful skills you can develop as a clinician.

Listen now and start seeing the optic disc in a whole new way. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and clinical resources.

episodes.title: Visual Field Testing in Glaucoma: 24-2, 10-2 & GHT Explained
episodes.description:
Ever wondered what those flashing lights and button presses during a visual field test actually reveal about your eye health? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down one of the most essential tools in glaucoma care — visual field testing — and make it genuinely easy to understand.

Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide, and it steals your peripheral vision so gradually that most people never notice until serious damage has already occurred. That is exactly why visual field testing matters so much. We walk you through the 24-2 test, which maps 54 points across the central 24 degrees of your visual field and remains the gold standard for detecting classic glaucomatous damage patterns like arcuate scotomas and nasal steps. Then we zoom in on the 10-2 test, which densely maps the critical central 10 degrees — the zone responsible for reading, face recognition, and sharp detail — an area the 24-2 can miss in early or advanced disease.

We also unpack the Glaucoma Hemifield Test, the built-in analysis that compares the upper and lower halves of your visual field to flag the asymmetric damage patterns characteristic of glaucoma. Think of it as the smoke detector on your visual field report.

Whether you are a glaucoma patient trying to understand your results, a student learning perimetry for the first time, or a clinician looking for a clearer way to explain these concepts, this episode delivers practical, clinically grounded insights you can actually use.

Listen now and visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes covering everything in eye health and vision science.

episodes.title: OCT in Glaucoma: RNFL, GCC & Progression Analysis Explained
episodes.description:
Can you detect glaucoma before your patient even notices something is wrong? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down one of the most powerful tools in modern ophthalmology — optical coherence tomography — and show you exactly how to use it to catch glaucoma early, track it accurately, and protect your patients' vision for the long term.

We start with the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), the gold-standard structural measurement in glaucoma care, and explain what the color-coded sectors actually mean — and where they can mislead you. Then we dive into the ganglion cell complex (GCC), exploring why macular analysis can sometimes detect glaucomatous damage even before peripapillary RNFL changes appear, and how focal loss volume and global loss volume help quantify the extent of damage.

But the real highlight of this episode is the progression graph — the most underutilized feature on an OCT printout and arguably the most important for long-term glaucoma management. We walk you through how trend analysis transforms isolated snapshots into a meaningful clinical story, what makes a progression flag trustworthy, and why signal strength can make or break your interpretation.

Whether you are a resident learning to read your first OCT report, an optometrist managing glaucoma suspects, or a seasoned clinician looking to sharpen your approach, this episode gives you practical, clinically grounded insights you can apply immediately.

Tune in, and you will never look at an OCT printout the same way again. For more clinical content and resources, visit us at Focuslinks.in.

episodes.title: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: Diagnosis & Risk Stratification
episodes.description:
Over 80 million people worldwide are living with glaucoma — and most don't even know it. Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness, yet it progresses silently, without pain or obvious warning signs. In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we break down everything clinicians need to know about diagnosing POAG and identifying who is truly at risk before irreversible damage occurs.

We walk through the three diagnostic pillars of POAG — optic nerve assessment, visual field analysis, and gonioscopy — explaining why each one is non-negotiable for an accurate diagnosis. You'll learn how to interpret cup-to-disc ratio asymmetry, recognize violations of the ISNT rule, identify classic visual field defect patterns like arcuate scotomas and nasal steps, and understand why OCT-based RNFL imaging is changing the game for early detection.

We also dive deep into risk stratification, covering the key findings from the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study, the role of central corneal thickness in IOP interpretation, and how factors like age, race, family history, myopia, and systemic conditions influence disease progression. You'll come away with a practical framework for setting target IOP, determining treatment intensity, and tailoring follow-up schedules to each patient's unique risk profile.

Whether you're a seasoned ophthalmologist or a trainee building your clinical foundation, this episode gives you the tools to approach POAG with greater confidence and precision.

Listen now, and if you find this episode valuable, share it with a colleague and leave us a review. Visit Focuslinks.in for more clinically focused eye health content.
